title: Air-gapped vendor dependency & upgrade guidance (draft)
body:
Draft: Air-gapped vendor dependency & upgrade guidance

Purpose:
This is a working draft describing recommended practices for producing a deterministic offline vendor bundle, validating artifacts, and a low-risk upgrade/cutover sequence for air-gapped/private deployments. Focus is on: container images, language packages (wheels, pip indices), OS packages, and optional model blobs.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target environments: VPC-hosted private control plane + on-prem worker clusters (air-gapped).
- Customers may have: isolated internal registries (Harbor/Quay), object storage with limited egress, and internal package caches.
- We assume access to a bastion host in a network that can reach public internet for initial mirror generation.
- This doc covers artifact collection, manifesting, terraform module knobs to support offline installs, and an upgrade cutover checklist.

High-level flow:
1) Define bundle manifest (list of images, packages, custom binaries).
2) Resolve transitive deps and collect exact digests/versions.
3) Mirror artifacts into staging (local registry + object store) and generate an index.
4) Produce SBOM + signed manifest and checksums.
5) Run preflight verification on an isolated validation cluster.
6) Ship to customer (or deliver as on-site media) and run install/upgrade workflow.

Artifact collection notes (practical):
- Images: always capture by digest (not tag). Example: registry.redwood.ai/model-server@sha256:abcd...
- Language packages: for Python capture wheels and a simple pip-index (static HTML + simplejson index). Record exact filenames + hashes.
- OS packages: prefer using distro-specific mirrors (apt: pool/, yum: repodata). If impossible, bundle the .deb/.rpm files with repodata regenerated on customer side where allowed.
- Model blobs: include manifest with model version, expected sha256, and size. Consider chunking large blobs and include resume metadata.
- Keys: store GPG public key(s) for verify; never embed private keys in the bundle.

Bundle manifest (recommended fields):
- version: v1
- created_by: redwood-airgap-generator/0.2
- created_at: 2024-11-12T10:34:00Z
- artifacts: [ list of entries, each entry = type|name|location|digest|size|sig ]
- sbom_uri: relative/path/sbom.json
- signatures: [ sig-by-gpg-keyid ]
- notes: free-text (known incompatibilities)

Verification and signing:
- Generate sha256 checksums for every file and include checksums.txt.
- Sign the manifest + checksums with the repo GPG key. Provide public key and verification steps in README.
- Produce SBOM (CycloneDX or SPDX) for each image and the whole bundle.

Terraform module integration notes (practical knobs):
- TF module variables to support airgap: mirror_registry (string), mirror_bucket (string), bundle_manifest_url (string), offline_mode (bool), allow_unverified_images (bool).
- Behavior: when offline_mode=true the deployment uses mirror_registry for all images and falls back to prepackaged local file system paths for language/OS packages.
- Suggested outputs: applied_manifest_digest, preflight_status_url, install_job_id.
- Helpful implementation pattern: centralize image/template rewrites in a small provider function (module rewriter) so we can map canonical image names to mirror_registry prefixed digests at plan-time.

Example tfvars (illustrative):
mirror_registry = "harbor.internal.redwood.local/library"
mirror_bucket = "s3://customer-internal-bundles/redwood-2024-11-12"
bundle_manifest_url = "s3://customer-internal-bundles/redwood-2024-11-12/manifest.json"
offline_mode = true

Automation snippets (notes):
- rsync --archive --partial --progress --files-from=artifact-list.txt remote:/public-registry/ ./mirror-root/
- skopeo copy docker://registry.redwood.ai/model-server@sha256:abcd docker://harbor.internal/... --dest-creds user:pass
- pip download -r requirements.txt -d ./wheelhouse --no-deps (then later rebuild index)

Registry layout recommendations:
- Keep a flat project per-deployment: harbor.company/redwood/<deployment-id>/... to avoid name collisions.
- Maintain a simple image index file mapping canonical names -> local digest URIs for the TF rewriter to consume.
- Use immutable tags (digest-only promotion) to simplify verification.

Bandwidth, storage & time planning (heuristic):
- Example small deployment (control-plane + 3 workers): ~12GB images + 2GB wheels + 8GB OS packages = ~22GB compressed.
- Medium deployment: ~60–120GB. Large (entire model zoo) can be multiple TBs.
- Mirroring time: network egress 200Mbps -> 22GB takes ~15min; 500GB takes ~5.5hrs. Add extra for retries and registry API rate limits.

Preflight and validation (must-run before customer install):
- Validate checksums and GPG sigs against provided public key.
- Verify all container digests present in local registry and pullable by digest.
- Run smoke docker-compose / k8s job that starts the control plane containers and runs basic API health checks (token/hello endpoints).
- Test package installs (pip install --no-index --find-links) on a staging host.
- Run a small inference job (if models included) on the staging cluster to validate KV cache and storage mounts.

Upgrade/cutover plan (staged):
1) Preflight (bundle verify, registry available, storage mounts).
2) Validation cluster deploy (same K8s version + kernel tunables). Run e2e smoke.
3) Canary on production: upgrade a subset of nodes or a single availability zone: run canary workload for 2–4 hours (depends on SLA).
4) Sweep rollout: incrementally upgrade remaining nodes in waves, monitoring latency, error rate, and token throughput.
5) Post-upgrade evaluation (metrics 24–72h depending on risk profile).

Rollback guidance:
- Always keep the previous bundle and registry snapshot accessible.
- Terraform: use blue/green or rolling-replace patterns; ensure previous image digests are still available in mirror_registry.
- DB migrations: avoid incompatible migrations during air-gap upgrade unless you have tested downgrade path. If impossible, schedule maintenance window and snapshot DBs.

Cutover checklist (working):
- [ ] Manifest produced and signed
- [ ] All artifacts mirrored into mirror_registry/object store
- [ ] SBOM generated and attached
- [ ] TF variables for offline_mode set and rewriter mapping uploaded
- [ ] Preflight smoke tests passed on validation cluster
- [ ] Customer acceptance for maintenance window
- [ ] Backup/snapshot of control plane and DBs completed

Known risks & mitigation:
- Missing transitive dep: capture pip/apt/yum dependency lists and include them; run install tests in staging.
- Large model transfer failures: use chunking and resumable uploads; consider physical media for TB-scale.
- Clock skew: ensure NTP/time sync on target hosts before verifying signatures.
- License issues: include license.txt for all 3rd-party components in bundle.

Open questions (for PD/PS):
- Do we want to standardize on Harbor vs Quay for offline registry recommendations? (tradeoffs: Harbor UI + replication vs Quay security features)
- Should we include a thin runtime-only image set (smaller) vs full developer image set? Who owns the size tradeoff?
- For customers with strict FIPS/HSM requirements, do we provide pre-signed images or guidance for re-signing?

Next steps (short term):
- Marco: prototype registry index generator that emits mapping.json and an immutable manifest (due 2024-11-22).
- Priya: add TF module variable docstrings and example rewriter code (due 2024-11-28).
- Ethan: draft customer-facing README for verifying bundle (due 2024-12-05).

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add example sbom snippet and sample verification script (sha256sum + gpg --verify)
- Confirm how Dedicated SKU customers prefer artifact delivery (s3 presigned vs on-site transfer)
- Add automation for incremental mirror updates (delta sync)

References and related tickets: see linked_artifacts.

-- end draft --

(Comments and edits welcome in-place; this is intentionally pragmatic and half-bulleted for quick iteration.)
